questions.question: A bottle is filled with liquid of which 4 parts are water and 5 parts are fruit extract. How much of the mixture must be drawn off and replaced with water so that the mixture may be half water and half fruit extract?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A bottle with 4 parts are water and 5 parts are fruit extract.

Water : fruit extract = 4 : 5

**Calculation:**

Ratio of water : fruit = 4: 5 

Let x litres of this liquid be replaced with water. 

As per the question,

⇒ (4-(4x/9) +x) = (5-(5x/9)) 

⇒ x = 9/10 

So, part of the mixture replaced = 9/10 × 1/9 = 1/10

** ∴ The correct option is 1**

questions.question: If a²+(1)/(a²)=(7)/(3), then what is the value of (a³-(1)/(a³))?
How much chicory, costing ₹100/kg should be added to 40 kg of coffee costing ₹45/kg so that the mixture will be worth ₹60/kg?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Chicory** to **Coffee** = (Mixture Price − Coffee Price) : (Chicory Price − Mixture Price)

Ratio = (60 − 45) : (100 − 60) = 15 : 40 = 3 : 8

Given, 8 units of **Coffee** = 40 kg ⇒ 1 unit = 5 kg

Quantity of **Chicory** = 3 units = 3 × 5 = 15 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 15 kg.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price of **Chicory** (C₁) = ₹100/kg

Cost price of **Coffee** (C₂) = ₹45/kg

Quantity of **Coffee** (Q₂) = 40 kg

Mean price of the **Mixture** (M) = ₹60/kg

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6af8eaf18f441214163359d616c945a6c326f4cc44e38cd26da3c6a2a7f2724c.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Quantity of Cheaper / Quantity of Dearer = (CP of Dearer − Mean Price) / (Mean Price − CP of Cheaper)

Alternatively: Q₁ / Q₂ = (M − C₂) / (C₁ − M)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Q₁ / 40 = (60 − 45) / (100 − 60)

⇒ Q₁ / 40 = 15 / 40

⇒ Q₁ = (15 ÷ 40) × 40

⇒ Q₁ = 15 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 15 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It is a rule that enables us to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at their respective prices must be mixed to produce a mixture of a specified price.

Weighted Average Formula

The mean price M can also be calculated as M = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) / (n₁ + n₂), where n represents quantity and x represents price.

Profit/Loss on Mixture

If a mixture is sold at a profit, first find the Cost Price of the mixture: CP = [100 / (100 + P%)] × SP, then apply the alligation rule.

questions.question: The cost of 3 cups and 5 plates is ₹1,080 and the cost of 2 cups and 4 plates is ₹840. Find the ratio of the cost of a cup to the cost of a plate.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

2 Cups + 4 Plates = 840 → 1 Cup + 2 Plates = 420.

Multiply by 3 ⇒ 3 Cups + 6 Plates = 1260.

Difference with (3 Cups + 5 Plates = 1080) ⇒ 1 Plate = 1260 − 1080 = 180.

Cost of 1 Cup = 420 − (2 × 180) = 420 − 360 = 60.

Ratio of Cup to Plate = 60 : 180 = 1 : 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 ∶ 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 3 cups and 5 plates = ₹1,080

Cost of 2 cups and 4 plates = ₹840

**Formula Used:**

Simultaneous Linear Equations: a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂

 
 3 Cups + 5 Plates
 
• 
 ₹1080
 
 2 Cups + 4 Plates
 
• 
 ₹840
 Ratio Required = Cost of Cup : Cost of Plate

Let the cost of one cup be C and the cost of one plate be P.

⇒ 3C + 5P = 1080 ... (i)

⇒ 2C + 4P = 840 ... (ii)

⇒ From (ii), C + 2P = 420 ⇒ C = 420 − 2P

⇒ Substitute C in (i): 3 × (420 − 2P) + 5P = 1080

⇒ 1260 − 6P + 5P = 1080

⇒ 1260 − P = 1080

⇒ P = 1260 − 1080 = 180

⇒ C = 420 − 2 × 180 = 420 − 360 = 60

⇒ Ratio C : P = 60 : 180

⇒ C : P = 1 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 1 ∶ 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

An equation of the form ax + by + c = 0 where a, b, and c are real numbers and a, b ≠ 0.

Ratio and Proportion

A ratio is a comparison of two quantities by division, denoted as a : b or a/b. It has no units if both quantities have the same unit.

Elimination Method

A method of solving simultaneous equations by making the coefficients of one variable equal to eliminate it by addition or subtraction.

questions.question: The length, breadth, and height of a room are 7 m, 5 m and 3 m, respectively. Find the cost of whitewashing the walls of the room and the ceiling at the rate of ₹16 per m².
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total area to paint = Area of 4 walls + Area of ceiling

Total area = 2 × h × (l + b) + (l × b)

Total area = 2 × 3 × (7 + 5) + (7 × 5) = 72 + 35 = 107 m²

Total Cost = 107 × 16 = ₹1,712

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,712.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length (l) = 7 m, Breadth (b) = 5 m, Height (h) = 3 m

Rate of whitewashing = ₹16 per m²

**Formula Used:**

Area of 4 walls (Lateral Surface Area) = 2h(l + b)

Area of ceiling = l × b

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a205cb136fcc4251132aeed39d770fdd00ddff73dad744a83415a499eb82bb3e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of 4 walls = 2 × 3 × (7 + 5) m²

⇒ Area of 4 walls = 6 × 12 = 72 m²

⇒ Area of ceiling = 7 × 5 = 35 m²

⇒ Total area to be whitewashed = 72 + 35 = 107 m²

⇒ Total Cost = Total Area × Rate per m²

⇒ Total Cost = 107 × 16 = 1712

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,712.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cuboid

Includes the area of all 6 rectangular faces: 2(lb + bh + hl).

Lateral Surface Area (Area of 4 walls)

Excludes the top (ceiling) and bottom (floor) faces: 2h(l + b).

Length of Longest Diagonal

The longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboidal room is its main diagonal: √(l² + b² + h²).
